Electrical Rule 1 (Playbook #1) — Diameter ↔ radius / area geometry slip

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 7 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Circular geometry questions almost always hide a diameter-versus-radius mistake. Area is A = pi*d^2/4. Candidates who treat the given diameter as a radius get areas four times too large (or stresses four times too small).

When to use

Circular section, shaft, hanger, pipe, or bolt with diameter given in mm.

Application steps

  1. Circle the numeric diameter in the stem and write r = d/2 on scratch paper.
  2. Compute A = pi*d^2/4 once; do not reuse a remembered 'pi r^2' with d plugged in as r.
  3. Strike any option that matches P/(pi*d^2), P/(pi*r), or 4x/0.25x of the correct stress.
  4. If net area of a plate with holes is asked, apply hole deductions after the correct gross area.
Memory cue: A = pi*d^2/4 ; sigma = P/A

Core elimination move

Compute A = πd²/4 (or r = d/2) once on scratch paper. Eliminate options that match P/(πd²), P/(πr), or treating d as r.

Below: all 7 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Subject: Power Systems

Stem: Corona loss on EHV lines increases most when:

  1. Conductor diameter is large and dry
  2. Bundled conductors always eliminate corona
  3. Surface voltage gradient is high and weather is foul
  4. Line is heavily loaded at unity pf
Elimination solution (this rule only) Elimination using Rule 1 — Diameter ↔ radius / area geometry slip When this rule fires: Circular section, shaft, hanger, pipe, or bolt with diameter given in mm. Core move: Compute A = πd²/4 (or r = d/2) once on scratch paper. Eliminate options that match P/(πd²), P/(πr), or treating d as r. Apply the rule in order: 1. Circle the numeric diameter in the stem and write r = d/2 on scratch paper. 2. Compute A = pi*d^2/4 once; do not reuse a remembered 'pi r^2' with d plugged in as r. 3. Strike any option that matches P/(pi*d^2), P/(pi*r), or 4x/0.25x of the correct stress. 4. If net area of a plate with holes is asked, apply hole deductions after the correct gross area. How the rule makes the key correct: Corona depends on gradient and air condition (Peek/Peterson). Option-by-option elimination: A) Conductor diameter is large and dry → STRIKE — Conductor diameter is large and dry: Larger D lowers gradient. B) Bundled conductors always eliminate corona → STRIKE — Bundled conductors always eliminate corona: Load pf affects losses not corona onset same way. C) Surface voltage gradient is high and weather is foul → KEEP — Survives this rule — matches the asked quantity and the rule’s correct path. D) Line is heavily loaded at unity pf → STRIKE — Line is heavily loaded at unity pf: Bundling reduces but does not always eliminate. Conclusion: after Rule 1 elimination, only C remains → keyed answer C.

Electrical Rule 2 (Playbook #5) — Per-unit base-change scaling

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 47 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Per-unit impedance scales with the chosen bases: Zpu = Zohm * Sbase / Vbase^2. Changing only Sbase scales Zpu in direct proportion.

When to use

Zpu / Xpu and base MVA or kV changes.

Application steps

  1. Note old and new Sbase and Vbase.
  2. If Sbase doubles and Vbase is unchanged, Zpu halves — strike 'unchanged', 'doubles', 'squared'.
  3. If Vbase also changes, recompute the full ratio.
Memory cue: Zpu = Zohm * Sbase / Vbase^2

Core elimination move

Zpu ∝ Sbase / Vbase². If Sbase doubles and Vbase fixed → Zpu halves. Eliminate ‘unchanged’, ‘doubles’, or ‘squared’ unless the stem changed Vbase too.

Below: all 47 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Subject: Power Systems

  1. 640
  2. 400

Elimination solution (this rule only) Elimination using Rule 5 — Per-unit base-change scaling When this rule fires: Zpu / Xpu and base MVA or kV changes. Core move: Zpu ∝ Sbase / Vbase². If Sbase doubles and Vbase fixed → Zpu halves. Eliminate ‘unchanged’, ‘doubles’, or ‘squared’ unless the stem changed Vbase too. Apply the rule in order: 1. Note old and new Sbase and Vbase. 2. If Sbase doubles and Vbase is unchanged, Zpu halves — strike 'unchanged', 'doubles', 'squared'. 3. If Vbase also changes, recompute the full ratio. How the rule makes the key correct: This is a Conceptual item in Power Systems (Conceptual). The keyed choice “√(L/C) and V²” is the only option consistent with the governing engineering behaviour for this micro-topic at APTRANSCO AEE depth. Core reason: SIL = V²/Zc, Zc=√(L/C). A prepared AEE candidate should recognise the concept quickly and still verify units / pu / boundary conditions before locking the option. Scratch check that confirms the survivor: Step-by-step working: SIL = V²/Zc, Zc=√(L/C). Verify units/pu bases and that the arithmetic lands on the keyed option “√(L/C) and V²” (Gate C). Final keyed result: √(L/C) and V² Option-by-option elimination: A) 640 → KEEP — Survives this rule — matches the asked quantity and the rule’s correct path. B) 400 → STRIKE — violates Rule 5 (Per-unit base-change scaling): classic distractor in this trap family / does not match the rule’s correct path. C) 250 → STRIKE — violates Rule 5 (Per-unit base-change scaling): classic distractor in this trap family / does not match the rule’s correct path. D) 160 → STRIKE — violates Rule 5 (Per-unit base-change scaling): classic distractor in this trap family / does not match the rule’s correct path. Conclusion: after Rule 5 elimination, only A remains → keyed answer A.

Electrical Rule 3 (Playbook #6) — Sequence-network connection by fault type

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 24 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Unsymmetrical faults require specific sequence-network connections. Memorising the four classic connections eliminates most wrong options instantly.

When to use

LG / LL / LLG / 3φ fault; options name sequence networks.

Application steps

  1. Identify fault type: 3-ph, LG, LL, LLG.
  2. 3-ph → positive only; LG → 1-2-0 in series; LL → 1 parallel 2; LLG → 1 series (2 parallel 0).
  3. Strike any option that omits a required sequence or uses only zero-sequence.
Memory cue: LG: Z1+Z2+Z0 ; LL: Z1||Z2 ; LLG: Z1+(Z2||Z0)

Core elimination move

3φ → positive only. LG → series 1-2-0. LL → 1 parallel 2. LLG → 1 series (2∥0). Eliminate any option that omits a required sequence or uses only zero-sequence.

Electrical Rule 4 (Playbook #7) — √3 / phase-factor forgotten

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 24 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Three-phase power and current conversions carry a root-3 factor. Forgetting it, or using 3 instead of root-3, produces the most common distractors.

When to use

3-phase power, line vs phase quantities, line current from kVA.

Application steps

  1. Write P = root3 * VL * IL * cos(phi) (or the form asked).
  2. Strike options that drop root3 or replace it with 3 without justification.
Memory cue: P = √3 · VL · IL · cosφ

Core elimination move

P = √3 VL IL cosφ. Eliminate options that drop √3 or use 3 instead of √3 (or vice versa) without stem justification.

Below: all 24 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Electrical Rule 5 (Playbook #8) — Thevenin / Norton source deactivation

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 17 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Thevenin/Norton resistance is found with independent sources deactivated: voltage sources shorted, current sources opened.

When to use

Req, RN, or Vth with independent sources in the figure.

Application steps

  1. For Req/RN, deactivate independent sources first.
  2. Strike options that leave sources 'on' while claiming equivalent resistance.
  3. Do not confuse Vth (open-circuit voltage) with RN.
Memory cue: Independent V → short; independent I → open; then find Req

Core elimination move

Independent voltage sources → short; current sources → open. Eliminate options that leave sources active while claiming Req/RN.

Below: all 17 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Electrical Rule 6 (Playbook #9) — Resonance / X_L = X_C identity

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 52 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

At series resonance XL = XC so net reactive part is zero and Z = R (minimum). Parallel resonance is the dual (impedance maximum).

When to use

Series/parallel RLC, ω0, or impedance at resonance.

Application steps

  1. Confirm series vs parallel from the figure/stem.
  2. At series resonance strike any option that still carries j(XL-XC) ≠ 0.
  3. Use omega0 = 1/√(LC) only when that is the ask.
Memory cue: Series resonance: XL = XC → Z = R

Core elimination move

Series resonance → Z = R (min). Parallel → Z max. Eliminate options that keep j(XL−XC) nonzero at the stated resonance.

Below: all 52 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Q1 of 52 · Electrical FLT-01 · data/electrical/ee-flt01.js#Q13 · Key A

Subject: Power Systems

Stem: In equal-area criterion, for a sudden load rejection on a machine, accelerating area is bounded by:

  1. Pm increase above Pe until δmax with equal decelerating area
  2. Only Pe curve below Pm forever
  3. Fault clearing angle alone with no Pm
  4. Inertia H only — angles irrelevant
Elimination solution (this rule only) Elimination using Rule 9 — Resonance / X_L = X_C identity When this rule fires: Series/parallel RLC, ω0, or impedance at resonance. Core move: Series resonance → Z = R (min). Parallel → Z max. Eliminate options that keep j(XL−XC) nonzero at the stated resonance. Apply the rule in order: 1. Confirm series vs parallel from the figure/stem. 2. At series resonance strike any option that still carries j(XL-XC) ≠ 0. 3. Use omega0 = 1/√(LC) only when that is the ask. How the rule makes the key correct: First-swing stability uses the equal-area criterion: accelerating area while Pm > Pe during/after the fault must be balanced by a decelerating area after clearing. If mechanical power Pm is raised, the accelerating region grows and the available decelerating region shrinks — δ must swing farther (to a new δmax) so the areas can still balance. That is exactly the keyed statement. Option-by-option elimination: A) Pm increase above Pe until δmax with equal decelerating area → KEEP — Survives this rule — matches the asked quantity and the rule’s correct path. B) Only Pe curve below Pm forever → STRIKE — Only Pe curve below Pm forever: That picture means continuous acceleration with no decelerating area — first-swing unstable. It is not the equal-area recovery description after a Pm increase. C) Fault clearing angle alone with no Pm → STRIKE — Fault clearing angle alone with no Pm: Clearing angle/time matters, but without relating Pm to the Pe curves you cannot judge whether decelerating area still exists after the Pm change. D) Inertia H only — angles irrelevant → STRIKE — Inertia H only — angles irrelevant: Inertia H scales how fast δ(t) moves; it does not replace the Pe–Pm equal-area test for whether a stable δmax exists. Conclusion: after Rule 9 elimination, only A remains → keyed answer A.

Elimination solution (this rule only) Elimination using Rule 9 — Resonance / X_L = X_C identity When this rule fires: Series/parallel RLC, ω0, or impedance at resonance. Core move: Series resonance → Z = R (min). Parallel → Z max. Eliminate options that keep j(XL−XC) nonzero at the stated resonance. Apply the rule in order: 1. Confirm series vs parallel from the figure/stem. 2. At series resonance strike any option that still carries j(XL-XC) ≠ 0. 3. Use omega0 = 1/√(LC) only when that is the ask. How the rule makes the key correct: Synchronous generator internal voltage on lagging pf exceeds terminal voltage. Assemble Ef = V + Ia(Ra + jXs). With Ra≈0, pf=0.8 lag: Ia=0.8−j0.6, jXs Ia=0.6+j0.8, Ef=1.6+j0.8, |Ef|=sqrt(1.6^2+0.8^2)=sqrt(3.2)≈1.79 ≈ 1.8 pu. Scratch check that confirms the survivor: Vt=1 pu, Ia=1 pu, Xs=1.0 pu, Ra≈0, cosφ=0.8, sinφ=0.6. Take V on real axis; Ia=0.8−j0.6. j Xs Ia = j(0.8−j0.6)=0.6+j0.8. Ef = 1 + 0.6 + j0.8 = 1.6 + j0.8. |Ef| = sqrt(2.56+0.64)=sqrt(3.2)≈1.789 ≈ 1.8 pu. Option-by-option elimination: A) 1.8 pu → KEEP — Survives this rule — matches the asked quantity and the rule’s correct path. Electrical Rule 7 (Playbook #10) — Sign / sense / tension–compression flip

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 60 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

Many options are numerically close but reverse tension/compression or reaction direction. Equilibrium sense is part of the answer.

When to use

Reactions, BMD jump, member force T/C, or direction in options.

Application steps

  1. Fix one free-body sign convention from the figure.
  2. Eliminate options with correct magnitude but wrong sense (T/C or up/down).
Memory cue: Sum Fx = 0, Sum Fy = 0, Sum M = 0 (sense matters)

Core elimination move

Fix one free-body sign convention from the figure. Eliminate options whose magnitude is right but sense (↑/↓, T/C) contradicts equilibrium.

Electrical Rule 8 (Playbook #11) — Figure-dependency: cover the figure test

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 199 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

If a figure is attached, the keyed answer usually depends on a labelled length, support, or curve. Solving from the stem alone is a dependency failure.

When to use

Stem says ‘shown’, ‘figure’, or options name Detail/Curve labels.

Application steps

  1. Read every dimension and support on the crop before picking.
  2. Strike options that ignore a labelled overhang, load, or curve name.
  3. If the stem names Detail/Curve labels, those labels must appear on the figure.
Memory cue: Cover-the-figure test: cannot answer correctly with figure hidden

Core elimination move

If you can pick the answer without the figure, stop — stem/figure mismatch. Otherwise eliminate options that ignore a labelled dimension, support, or curve on the crop.

Below: all 199 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Electrical Rule 9 (Playbook #15) — SCR / PE latching vs holding vs firing

Stream section: Electrical · Questions in this section: 20 (every matching evidence item is solved below — none skipped)

What this rule means

For SCRs, latching current is larger than holding current. Latching is needed to establish conduction after the gate pulse; holding keeps it on.

When to use

Thyristor/SCR gate, latching, holding, or commutation options.

Application steps

  1. Remember IL > IH.
  2. Strike options that swap latching with holding or that size gate width from holding alone.
Memory cue: Latching current > holding current

Core elimination move

Latching > holding; latching is the current to *establish* conduction after gate pulse. Eliminate options that swap latching↔holding or that set gate width from holding current alone.

Below: all 20 questions for this rule in the Electrical stream, one after another. Each solution uses only this elimination rule.

Apply the rule in order: 1. Remember IL > IH. 2. Strike options that swap latching with holding or that size gate width from holding alone.
